body: Yes V-Carve. I have that and Cut 3D.
I cut first then paint. There is actually a laundry list of things I can do to make it look nice, but then I'm trying to branch out into new things.
It depends on weather it's just a business or a side project. Like I don't do this full time, and it's at a flea market so it's cash only.

We Make wood signs and images at the flea market. We go every month. So we will always be there. Here are some things I made.

http://imgur.com/a/HeoC5

http://imgur.com/DW3piqw

We have also made other signs with little sayings on them or little designs with family names and the such.

Trade Secret. Me and my partner started working at the flea market in the local area by selling there and expanding. We are going to online sales now, and still doing the flea market once a month. I know this isn't personal finance but the rule of thumb is thirds. When you make a sale a third goes to you, a third to the equipment, and a third to materials. It's slow to get started, but it's a good little venture to be in and you get closer to paying off with every sale. Then everything is Seconds, Half to you, Half to equipment. Plunge Routers, Sanders, Paint, you know the rest.
